blocks.x: If you were to give me a quick lesson in the phrasing of the different eras, what would you say? Like, say, from the ’20s versus the ’30s versus the ’40s.

In the ’20s and the ’30s, I think the music that evolved then was influenced more by the military thing, the marches, because martial music was very popular prior to that. Then, after that, you had the romantic jazz music that came along. It was more commercial. Then, from that, it began to get – the jazz thing began to get a little smoother, instead of – not so much syncopation – hard syncopation and so forth. I think that’s basically what they did. People decided, “I don’t” – “It sounds” – they wouldn’t say “corny.” They would probably say, “It sounds dated. It sounds old-fashioned.” Then deliberately they would try to find ways of playing the same in a different manner, so that it did sound different.
Then in the ’50s bebop came along and things got turned around again.
